blocks.text: 3.1. Framework and parameters setting. In this part, we consider the parameters appearing in eqs. (1.5) and (1.6) and deﬁne the ranges where they vary. In doing that, we take advantage of the estimates provided in [36] for prostate cancer treated with androgen deprivation therapy (ADT). We recall that the analysis in [36] relied on the results of the trial described in [11]. There, a cohort of patients with biochemical recurrence of the tumor (non-metastatic and castration sensitive, m0CSPC) after radical radiotherapy treatment underwent intermittent ADT.

Parameters not aﬀected by uncertainty. We begin by listing the parameters that in our experiments are assumed to be unaﬀected by uncertainty. The ﬁrst crucial quantity to be estimated is the proliferation rate for sensitive cells rS, which is employed to perform the time-normalization of the original system (1.2) into (1.5). In [36], the authors set rS = 0.027 day−1, adopted from a previous estimate derived in [40]. Then, the eﬀectiveness of the therapy is encoded in the value of the non-dimensional constant dˆD, which is set dˆD = 1.5 in [36] (see also [38] for the original estimate). We recall that the normalized dimension of the tumor is expressed using n = n(τ), which ranges in [0, 1]. Here, n = 0 means that the tumor cells (sensitive and resistant) are entirely extinct, while n = 1 implies that the tumor size has reached the system’s carrying capacity. The initial size of the tumor n(0) = n0 in our experiments takes values in {0.25, 0.50, 0.75} ∋ n0. We insist that n0 is not aﬀected by uncertainty, and we shall run the simulations separately for the diﬀerent values of n0. Finally, in [36] the turnover rate dˆT is proposed to range in the interval dˆT ∈ [0, 0.5]. In the present paper, we consider the most adverse scenario, i.e., we always set dˆT = 0.
